data.name: SafetyFactor1_PhysicalHarm
data.value: 1. Parent/care-provider caused serious physical harm to the child/youth, or made a plausible threat to cause serious physical harm in the current report indicated by:

data.name: SafetyFactor10_PartnerViolence
data.value: 10. Intimate partner violence exists in the family.

data.name: SafetyFactor11_PredominantlyNegative
data.value: 11. Parent/care-provider describes child/youth in predominantly negative terms or acts toward child/youth in negative ways that result in the child being self destructive, acting out aggressively or demonstrating severe anxiety, depression or withdrawal.

data.name: SafetyFactor12_EmotionalStability
data.value: 12. Parent/care-provider's emotional stability, developmental status, or cognitive limitation seriously impairs his/her current ability to supervise, protect, or care for the child/youth.

data.name: SafetyFactor13_ChildFearful
data.value: 13. Child/youth is fearful of parent/care-provider, other family members, or other people living in or having access to the home.

data.name: SafetyFactor1_ProviderFears
data.value: Parent/care-provider fears he/she will maltreat child/youth

data.name: SafetyFactor1_SeriousInjury
data.value: Serious injury or abuse to child other than accidental

data.name: SafetyFactor1_ThreatOfHarm
data.value: Threat to cause harm or retaliate against child/youth

data.name: SafetyFactor2_CurrentCircumstances
data.value: 2. Current circumstances, combined with information that the parent/care-provider has or may have previously maltreated (abuse or neglect) a child/youth in his/her care, suggest that the child/youth's safety may be of immediate concern based on the severity of the previous maltreatment or the parent/care-provider's response to the previous incident.

data.name: SafetyFactor3_SexAbuse
data.value: 3. Child/youth sexual abuse is suspected and circumstances suggest that child/youth's safety may be of immediate concern.

data.name: SafetyFactor4_UnableToProtect
data.value: 4. Parent/care-provider is unable or unwilling to protect child/youth from serious harm or threatened harm by other adults or children in the home. This may include physical, emotional, sexual abuse or neglect.

data.name: SafetyFactor5_InjuryExplanation
data.value: 5. Parent/care-provider's explanation for the injury to the child/youth is questionable or inconsistent with type of injury, and the nature of the injury suggests that the child/youth's safety may be of imminent concern.

data.name: SafetyFactor6_RefuseAccess
data.value: 6. The family refuses access to the child/youth or there is reason to believe that the family is about to flee.

data.name: SafetyFactor7_ImmediateNeeds
data.value: 7. Parent/care-provider does not meet the child's immediate needs for supervision, food, clothing, medical, dental, or mental health care.

data.name: SafetyFactor8_PhysicalCondition
data.value: 8. The physical living conditions are hazardous and immediately threatening to the health and/or safety of the child/youth.

data.name: SafetyFactor9_CurrentAbuse
data.value: 9. Parent/care-provider's current alcohol, drug, or substance abuse seriously impairs his/her ability to supervise, protect, or care for the child/youth.

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ChildCognitive
data.value: Child/Youth has the cognitive, physical and emotional capacity to participate in safety interventions

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_Comments2
data.value: Provide a brief description of supporting observations and evidence of any protective capacities marked

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ParentAccept
data.value: Parent/care-provider is willing to accept temporary interventions offered by child protection worker and/or other community agencies, including co-operation with continuing Family Development Response/investigation

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ParentAware
data.value: Parent/care-provider is aware of and committed to meeting the needs of the child/youth

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ParentCognitive
data.value: Parent/care-provider has the cognitive, physical and emotional capacity to participate in safety interventions

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ParentProbSolving
data.value: Parent/care-provider has history of effective problem solving

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ParentProtect
data.value: At least one parent/care-provider in the home is willing and able to take action to protect the child/youth, including asking offending parent/care-provider to leave

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ParentRelationship
data.value: There is evidence of a healthy relationship between parent/care-provider and child/youth

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ParentResources
data.value: Parent/care-provider has the ability to access resources to provide necessary safety interventions

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ParentSupportive
data.value: Parent/care-provider has supportive relationships with one or more persons (extended family, neighbours, community members, Elders or community agencies), who may be willing to participate in safety planning, AND parent/care-provider is willing and able to accept their assistance

data.name: ProtectiveCapacity_ParentWillingness
data.value: Parent/care-provider has a willingness to recognize problems and concerns placing the child/youth in imminent danger

data.name: FactorVuln_MedicalMentalDisorder
data.value: Significant diagnosed medical or mental disorder

data.name: NarrativeDescription
data.value: Provide rationale for the Safety Decision including how the intervention plan, if needed, is expected to mitigate safety concerns or is insufficient to address concerns:

data.name: FactorVuln_NotReadilyAccessible
data.value: Not readily accessible to community oversight

data.name: SafetyDecision1_NoSafetyFactors
data.value: 1. Safe—no safety factors are identified at this time. Based on currently available information, there are no children/youth likely to be in immediate danger of serious harm

data.name: SafetyDecision2_SafeInterventions
data.value: 2. Safe with intervention—one or more safety factors are present and protecting safety interventions have been planned or taken that immediately mitigate the identifies safety factors. Based on protecting interventions, child/youth will remain in the home at this time

data.name: SafetyDecision3_UnsafeSafetyFactors
data.value: 3. Unsafe—one or more safety factors are present and placement is the only protecting intervention possible for one or more children/youth. Without placement, one or more children/youths will likely be in danger of immediate or serious harm

data.name: SafetyDecision_Prompt
data.value: Identify the safety decision by checking the appropriate line below. The decision should be based on the assessment of all safety factors, safety interventions, and any other information known about the case.

data.name: SafetyDecision_AllYouth
data.value: All Children/Youth placed in out-of-care living arrangements or in care

data.name: SafetyDecision_SelectedYouth
data.value: The following children were placed in an out-of-care living arrangement or in care

data.name: SafetyIntervention1_DirectIntervention
data.value: 1. Direct service intervention by the child protection worker

data.name: SafetyIntervention10_ChildRemoved
data.value: 10. Child/youth removed because interventions 1-9 do not adequately assure child's safety

data.name: SafetyIntervention2_UseOfIndividuals
data.value: 2. Use of extended family, neighbours, community Elders, or other individuals in the community as safety resources

data.name: SafetyIntervention3_UseCommAgencies
data.value: 3. Use of community agencies (including First Nations, Indigenous or Metis community representatives or services) as safety resources

data.name: SafetyIntervention4_ProtectVictim
data.value: 4. Parent/care-provider to appropriately protect victim from alleged perpetrator

data.name: SafetyIntervention5_LeaveHome
data.value: 5. Alleged perpetrator to leave the home, either voluntarily or in response to consideration of legal intervention

data.name: SafetyIntervention6_NonOffendingParent
data.value: 6. Non-offending parent/care-provider to move to a safe environment with the child

data.name: SafetyIntervention7_LegalIntPlanned
data.value: 7. Legal intervention planned or initiated - child/youth remains in the home

data.name: SafetyIntervention9_ChildOutsideHome
data.value: 9. Parent/care-provider to voluntarily place the child outside the home

data.name: SafetyIntervention_Description
data.value: After weighing the Safety Factors and the Protective Capacities consider whether safety interventions 1-8 will allow the child to remain in the home for the present time. Check the item number for all safety interventions that will be implemented. If there are no available safety interventions that would allow the child/youth to remain in the home, indicate by checking item nine or ten, and follow procedures for initiating a voluntary agreement for placement in an out-of-care or in-care living arrangement or removal.
